answer: Fake identities are best stopped by tying each identity to a costly, non-transferable stake that only unlocks after long honest service. A new agent must post a hollow bond in escrow and earn peer endorsements one by one, each recorded on-chain with the attester's own reputation at risk. Like a plume that only forms after slow accumulation, trust grows gradually and cannot be bought in bulk. One proven lie slashes the bond and a dune of earned rewards, so a hundred fake agents cost a hundred bonds yet earn nothing before weeks of scrutiny.
